title: One-Dimensional Motion
learning_goal: Analyze one-dimensional motion using distance, displacement, speed, velocity, reference frames, and acceleration.

stages.title: 1. Start from the beginning
stages.content: Motion tells us how an object's position changes. Distance is the total path traveled, while displacement is the change from starting position to ending position and includes direction.

stages.title: 2. Build your confidence
stages.content: Speed tells how fast an object moves. Velocity tells both how fast and in what direction. A positive velocity means motion in the chosen positive direction; a negative velocity means motion in the opposite direction.

stages.title: 3. Teaching guide
stages.content: A runner moves from x = 2 m to x = 14 m in 4 s. First find displacement: Δx = 14 − 2 = 12 m. Then divide by elapsed time: v = Δx/Δt = 12/4 = 3 m/s. The positive sign tells us the runner moved in the positive direction.

stages.title: 4. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A cart moves from x = 10 m to x = 2 m in 4 s. What is its average velocity?
stages.hint: Start with displacement. Subtract initial position from final position and keep the sign.
stages.alternate_explanation: Picture a number line. The cart moves from 10 toward 2, so its displacement points in the negative direction before you divide by time.

stages.title: 5. Practice by yourself
stages.prompt: A cyclist moves from x = −4 m to x = 20 m in 6 s. What is the cyclist's average velocity?
stages.hint: Find Δx = x_f − x_i first, then divide by 6 s.
stages.alternate_explanation: On a number line, count the signed change from −4 to 20, then spread that change evenly across 6 seconds.

stages.title: 6. Extend the idea
stages.content: Acceleration is the rate at which velocity changes. An object accelerates when it speeds up, slows down, or changes direction. Average acceleration is a = Δv/Δt.

stages.title: 7. Build mastery
stages.content: When you are ready, solve new problems that mix distance, displacement, speed, velocity, reference frames, and acceleration without being shown the method first.

practice.intro: Practice Mode skips the teaching sequence and gives you one problem at a time. Submit an answer, get feedback, then move to a new problem.

problems.prompt: A car moves from x = 5 m to x = 29 m in 8 s. What is its average velocity?
problems.hint: Find the signed displacement first, then divide by 8 s.
problems.alternate_explanation: The car changes position by 24 m over 8 seconds. Think of average velocity as equal position change per second.

problems.prompt: A student walks from x = 12 m to x = −6 m in 9 s. What is the average velocity?
problems.hint: Final position is less than initial position, so the displacement should be negative.
problems.alternate_explanation: Draw the two positions on a number line. The student moves 18 m in the negative direction over 9 seconds.

problems.prompt: A train has an initial velocity of 4 m/s and reaches 16 m/s in 6 s. What is its average acceleration?
problems.hint: Use change in velocity divided by elapsed time.
problems.alternate_explanation: The velocity increases by 12 m/s across 6 seconds, so ask how much velocity is added each second.
